newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia seeks help from above in drug war.
newsitem.headline: Colombia seeks help from above in drug war.

text.p: Justice Minister Carlos Medellin will fly to Paris on Tuesday for talks aimed at contracting a French spy-in-the-sky satellite to monitor Colombia's illicit drug crops, government officials said on Monday.

They said Medellin would be accompanied by Col. Leonardo Gallego, head of the anti-narcotics division of the National Police, and Joaquin Polo, director of the presidential office on counternarcotics.

Government officials announced plans to contract a French satellite earlier this month after angrily rejecting a U.S. report that Colombia's production of coca leaf -- the raw material for cocaine -- increased by 32 percent last year.

The increase, which made Colombia the world's second largest producer of coca, was cited among other reasons for Washington's decision last month to leave Colombia on a blacklist of countries that have failed to cooperate fully in global anti-drug efforts.

Police and government officials, including Medellin, have argued that the U.S. report failed to take into account the vast tracts of coca fields that were eradicated through aerial spraying with herbicides.

Foreign Minister Maria Emma Mejia said in an interview with national radio over the weekend that a satellite contracted through a third country, preferrably France, would help provide Colombia with independent verification of U.S. drug crop estimates.
Colombia, the world's top producer of cocaine, has also become a leading producer of heroin. Its U.S.-backed aerial spraying programme targets fields of opium poppy as well as coca.
